correctness.rationale: A vanishing pure fourth-power coefficient makes the corresponding vertex singular. Thus A=1 is a unique scalar representative. On a coordinate line a nonvertex singularity corresponds to a null vector of its binary principal block; with nonzero diagonal a singular block has a null vector with both coordinates present. If the binary blocks are nonsingular, any nonzero null vector of the full symmetric matrix has all coordinates nonzero. Over the algebraic closure its coordinates lift by square roots, and the gradient of Q(X²,Y²,Z²) vanishes exactly by the supported block equations. This proves the geometric criterion. For the Cartier/Hasse–Witt calculation the precise semilinear operation cubes the Laurent representative and then multiplies by the equation squared. Mixed basis transitions require an odd exponent, while the three even diagonal target exponents give twice f+de, be+df and cd+ef, respectively. Perfection and diagonality keep the support unchanged under Frobenius iteration, so r is the number of nonzero entries and a=3−r. For the total count there are (q−1)^4 admissible choices of b,c,d,e before f; each of the two excluded f-square equations removes (q−1)^4+(q−1)^2, since the one-pair character sums are −(q−1) and −(q−1)χ(−1) and the double sums factor. Their intersection has (q−1)^2 cases with d=e=0, none with exactly one nonzero, and (q−1)^2(q−2) with both nonzero: normalization by d and e gives w=u+v and (u−v)²=0 in characteristic 3. For prescribed j diagonal zeros, T₁=(q−1)^2(q²−3q+3) since f=−de and with d,e nonzero one takes u,v nonzero, not 1, with uv≠1. T₂=(q−1)^3 because e(b−d²)=0 forces e=f=0, and T₃=(q−1)^2 because d must then vanish. Coordinate permutations followed by rescaling make the stated inclusion-exclusion valid for each prescribed set of j positions. This recovers all four polynomials including 3-rank zero through three over F₃ and F₉. An independent bounded replay enumerated b,c in F_q^× and d,e,f in F_q at q=3,9 (F₉=F₃[u]/(u²+1)), formed M with diagonals 1,b,c and off-diagonals −d,−e,−f, filtered by its three binary principal minors and determinant, and grouped by the number of nonzero off-diagonal minors. It returned (4,12,0,0) and (64,1344,8064,19584). No uploaded code was run; the finite replay is not a replacement for the all-q proof.

originality.rationale: Bounded pass for the complete rank-refined distribution over every extension in the fixed-coordinate scalar-only quotient. Credit exact indexed overlap for the total smooth count and the entire F₃ specialization, and related all-extension counts in the A=B=C=1 slice. The normalized slice or geometric superspecial classification does not count all rational marked coefficient classes. residual_risks: Brock's original superspecial enumeration was not inspected; it could cover the rank-zero component under a related convention.

value.rationale: A uniform rank stratification of a natural finite-field coefficient family quantifies the smooth nonordinary locus and shows exactly when ordinary members occur among all marked equations. The result gives arithmetic information not recoverable from the known total smooth count or a table of small-field or isomorphism-class representatives. The fixed-coordinate convention is essential for using the counts as a coefficient census rather than a moduli mass.
